outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) The EPUB3 label in the agent output omits the trailing exclamation mark shown in the DOM (“EPUB3 ★ Recommended for most devices !”); this is minor and does not affect the availability determination. 

Critical issues: (1) Release Date is reported as “Jun 1, 1998,” but the provided DOM snapshots do not show any “Release Date” label/value at all, so this value is unsupported and may be fabricated or taken from memory rather than the required labeled field. (2) Last Update is reported as “Sep 1, 2026,” and similarly there is no “Last Update” label/value visible in the DOM; additionally, this date is highly suspect and unsupported. Because the task explicitly requires using the Release Date and Last Update labels on the Project Gutenberg page and preserving the displayed dates exactly, unsupported/possibly invented values for these two fields are outcome-critical failures.

What the agent did accomplish: The agent was on the correct Gutenberg page (https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1342). The author “Austen, Jane, 1775-1817” and language “English” are supported by the metadata table in DOM state 1. The availability of all three named formats is supported: DOM state 1 shows links for “EPUB3 ★ Recommended for most devices !”, “Plain Text (accessible)”, and “Download HTML (zip)”, and the action history shows only scrolling (no downloads). 

Overall outcome: Despite correctly identifying the page, author, language, and the three format availabilities, the agent failed the task’s core requirement of accurately recording Release Date and Last Update from the Gutenberg-labeled fields. Since two of the four required metadata fields are not reliably captured and appear invented/unsupported, an average user would not consider the task successfully completed.

A reasonable user would be flexible about minor punctuation, but not flexible about incorrect or fabricated dates or failing to use the Gutenberg-labeled Release Date/Last Update fields.
